name: Grandmaster Flash
hook: Worked out how to extend a drum break by hand, then named and taught the whole vocabulary of turntablism.

blurb.age7: Flash figured out how to use two record players to keep just the drum part playing over and over, by hand.
blurb.age13: In the mid-1970s Flash developed 'quick mixing,' cueing and cutting between two copies of the same record by ear and by hand, so a DJ could extend a short drum break indefinitely and cut precisely on the beat. He later formalized and named several of the core turntablist techniques and recorded some of the first records to document them directly.
blurb.adult: Flash's technical contribution is specific and verifiable: cueing by placing a finger on the record and back-cueing, cutting cleanly between two copies of a break, and later scratching, techniques he is widely credited with systematizing even though sound system and mobile DJ culture in the Bronx was collectively inventive rather than the work of one person alone.

signatureTracks.title: The Adventures of Grandmaster Flash on the Wheels of Steel
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A single continuous turntable performance, cutting across multiple records, recorded essentially as documentation of a live DJ set.

signatureTracks.title: The Message
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Credited to Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five, though largely written and performed by Melle Mel and Sugar Hill's in-house talent. Shifted hip-hop's subject matter toward direct social commentary.
